basic_identification.full_title: Periodic Inspection and Testing — Welded Low Carbon Steel Cylinders Exceeding 5-Litre Water Capacity for Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) — Code of Practice (आवधिक निरीक्षण एवं परीक्षण — द्रवित पेट्रोलियम गैस (एलपीजी) के लिए 5-लीटर से अधिक जल क्षमता वाले वेल्डित अल्प कार्बन इस्पात के सिलिंडर — रीति संहिता)
basic_identification.sector_category: Mechanical Engineering / Gas Cylinders (approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Gas Cylinders Sectional Committee, MED 16, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This Indian Standard specifies the mandatory periodic inspection, quality evaluation, physical testing, safety re-qualification, and record-keeping procedures for transportable, refillable welded low-carbon steel LPG cylinders of water capacity exceeding 5 litres up to and including 250 litres.

version_status_and_amendments.supersedes: None (Formulated as an independent periodic code of practice to separate operational maintenance from manufacturing specifications)

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Procedural Code of Practice / Safety and Testing Guidelines (Mechanical Engineering Department / Gas Cylinders)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Mandatory Certification and Procedural Compliance under the Gas Cylinder Rules of the Government of India, in direct coordination with the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO). Cylinder testing stations must be officially approved by PESO and certified by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) to execute periodic inspections. Cylinders passing all tests must be stamped with the testing station's unique identification mark and the new test date on the stay plate/collar stay before returning to commercial filling rotation.

requirements.detail: Following external and internal cleaning of the cylinder body, the cylinder must be weighed on a calibrated scale. If the cylinder has lost more than 5 percent of its original stamped tare weight, it must be rejected.
Valve pad threads must be thoroughly cleaned of paint and residue using a soft wire brush and checked in accordance with IS 9121 using a standard 3/4" 14 NGT thread plug gauge.

Every cylinder that passes the visual inspections must be subjected to a hydrostatic proof pressure test at a test pressure of 2.45 MPa (25.00 kgf/cm²). The test pressure must be held with zero drop or leakage.

Following successful completion of the hydrostatic test, all residual testing water must be drained, and air must be removed by press-opening the valve using a suitable adaptor. Storing any cylinder with internal air pressure is strictly prohibited.

Establishes a strict visual rejection framework for physical defects on the cylinder wall under Table 1, including bulges, dents, cuts, digs, cracks, laminations, and foot ring bottom clearance limits.
A bulge (visible swelling) or a crack (split or rift in the shell) compromises structural safety. Rejection is mandatory in all cases.

A dent (localized depression) requires rejection if its depth exceeds 1/10th of its mean diameter, its mean diameter exceeds 1/4th of the cylinder diameter, or if it lies on or adjacent to a weld joint.
A cut or gouge requires rejection if its length is 75 mm or more, or if the remaining wall thickness in the affected portion is less than the minimum calculated wall thickness.
A dig (surface penetration) requires rejection if its length is 75 mm or more and its width is 4 mm or more.

Footring bottom clearance (distance of body bottom from the ground) must not be less than 8 mm for cylinders up to 34 litres water capacity, 15 mm for cylinders between 34 to 50 litres, and 25 mm for cylinders exceeding 50 litres.

Establishes maximum depth limits for corrosion. Isolated pits, area corrosion (not exceeding 20% surface), line corrosion, and crevice corrosion require rejection if the depth of penetration exceeds 0.4 mm.

Cylinders passing inspection must be stamped on the valve collar stay plate in the format '09 A - XX', where '09' represents the year of testing, 'A' indicates the month (A=Jan, B=Feb, etc.), and 'XX' represents the monthly control number.
All inspection, visual, hydrostatic, and pneumatic testing logs must be digitally recorded and maintained in a computerized database for the entire operational life of the cylinder.

Observed or calculated dimensions, defect depths, weights, and test pressures must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 16054 : 2013 is the primary national Indian Standard code of practice prescribing the mandatory procedures for the periodic inspection, testing, and safety re-certification of welded low-carbon steel LPG cylinders (exceeding 5-litre water capacity up to 250 litres). Developed under Sectional Committee MED 16 and reaffirmed in 2024, the standard unifies safety re-qualification in India. It mandates executing a hydrostatic proof pressure test at 2.45 MPa, enforces a strict visual inspection table (Table 1) to reject cylinders carrying structural defects (such as bulges, cracks, deep dents, or corrosion pits deeper than 0.4 mm), rejects cylinders with tare weight losses exceeding 5%, requires stamping the stay plate with a standardized year-month date code (e.g., 09 A - XX), and requires all testing stations to record and maintain active test certificates digitally on computers for the entire service life of each cylinder.
